newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sydney voted "world's best city" for second time.
newsitem.headline: Sydney voted "world's best city" for second time.

text.p: The future Olympic city of Sydney has been voted the world's top city for the second straight year in a survey of American travellers, Australian tourism officials said on Tuesday.
They said the accolade had been awarded after Travel & Leisure magazine's annual reader survey which also saw another Australian city, Melbourne, make the top five.
The top five cities in the survey were Sydney, Florence, Rome, San Francisco and Melbourne.

"For U.S. travellers to have voted two Australian cities in the top five best cities in the world confirms Australia's growing reputation as one of the world's premier holiday destinations," said John Morse, managing director of the Australian Tourist Commission.
"Research over the past few years has consistently shown Australia to be the number one ideal and preferred destination for potential travellers from the U.S.," Morse added.

According to official statistics, over 320,000 Americans visited Australia in the year ending May 1997, representing 7.5 percent of all international arrivals. They stayed an average of 22 nights and contributed almost A$1.4 billion (US$1.0 billion) in foreign exchange earnings.
Morse said that the ATC was trying to use the increased international attention generated by Sydney's hosting of the 2000 Olympic Games and the survey was a sign of its success.
